items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: And then formed a little group of my own. With Barney B. Godd on tenor we were learning in Saxton. And Louie Russell, Paul Barberin, Willie Santiago, Alnorma Twai on trumpet.

ctx.x: Can you tell us something about your training and taking lessons and so on?

Well, I started taking lessons around 9 years of age with my uncle, Wooden Joe Nicholas. He was my big influence on this jazz scene. And later on, I went to Papa Teo and took lessons with him for about a couple of years. Then Lorenzo Teo, his son. And finished up with him until around 1915. Then I started to go pro. My first gigs around New Orleans was with the Maple Leaf Band. Then Buddy Petite's Band. When Jimmy Noon left to go to Chicago, I played with Buddy Petite and several other bands around New Orleans.…

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1960-01-28
items.q: Well, he took the clarinet while we were working at Tom Anderson. He and Albert Nicholas team were together.

ctx.x: When did he take up the clarinet?

Well, he took the clarinet while we were working at Tom Anderson. He and Albert Nicholas team were together. He played like a flute at that time. He used to call him Snake Chalmers. He used to call him. He used to kill him all the time. Albert Nicholas used to laugh at him all the time. So I told him, don't pay attention about laughing at him. Just continue trying to play his horn. Keep on practicing. Well, that guy came up very fast. When he was in King Oliver's band, he started featuring the clarinet. He…
Did he ever play clarinet at all with Oliver?

items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: I had a band at Tom Anderson on Ramport and Canal.

ctx.x: What about Rudy Jackson? Was he around?

That's right. I played with him in the band also. You see, I came before Bonnie and Paul. Joe said for me in 23. I had a band at Tom Anderson on Ramport and Canal. On Ramport and I was there. And Jimmy Noon came down from Mardi Gras. And we had a hell of a band then. And Bonnie, we were just running sax, you know. And Bonnie was playing ten. I was playing alto and clarinet.
